Numeric values of capability, exception-type, idle-state, timing and fault constants used by the fragments.
Full layouts of trap frame, CPUID leaf and decoded instruction structures beyond referenced members.
Contracts of generic checksum, generic user copy and user-access window primitives.

findings.text: Kernel destination machine-check tolerant copy selects among fragile, fast-string and plain paths using a flag and a CPU capability, and reports the count not transferred with zero meaning complete.

User destination machine-check tolerant copy mirrors the kernel path choice but brackets fragile and fast-string transfers in a user-access window and falls back to a generic user copy when the capability is absent.

Fragile copy aligns the source to eight bytes with single-byte moves, transfers a middle run in eight-byte units, then drains a trailing byte run, returning zero on full success and a computed remainder on fault.

Fragile copy assigns machine-check safe handlers to read positions and plain handlers to write positions; read faults fold remaining whole units plus trailing length into the result while whole-unit write faults divert to a separate tail routine.
Enhanced fast-string copy moves the requested length with a single repeat string operation, returns zero on success, and on fault returns the hardware-updated remaining count.
Enhanced fast-string copy has one machine-check safe fixup that converts a fault during the repeat move into a short-transfer remainder for generic and user copy callers.
One build variant provides an empty fragile enabler and defines the fragile-enabled predicate as always false, forcing callers onto capability or fallback paths.

Register-based page copy transfers one page in 64-byte strides using eight general registers, prefetches ahead during the bulk phase, then completes a short non-prefetched phase and restores saved state.
Page copy length is 4096 bytes organized as sixty-four 64-byte blocks with a bulk phase covering all but five blocks.

User move alternative dispatches on length: tiny lengths use a byte loop, medium lengths use an eight-byte loop that falls back to bytes, large lengths select between repeat-byte and aligned repeat-word plus remainder handling.
Every faultable access in the user move alternative has a user-exception entry resuming at a byte-wise tail or at exit, reconstructing remaining length from word count and remainder where needed.
Family, model and stepping accessors are provided for both packed signatures and CPUID leaf structures.
Extended family adds only when base equals fifteen; extended model merges with a four-bit shift only when family reaches six; stepping is the low nibble of the signature.
IP checksum helper computes a partial sum over a buffer with zero initial value and folds it to the final sixteen-bit result.
Checksum plus user-copy wrappers may sleep, validate the user range and return zero on validation failure, otherwise perform a generic checksummed copy under an explicit user-access window.
Unchecked checksummed copy forwards directly to the generic checksummed copy without validation or window management.
Delay core indirects through a main pointer defaulting to a loop and a halt helper pointer; selectors switch the main pointer to timestamp polling or to halt mode paired with one of two idle helpers.

Timestamp delay runs with preemption disabled while sampling an ordered counter, briefly enables around a pause to permit real-time progress, and rebalances remaining cycles plus baseline if the CPU changes.
Loop delay consumes the supplied iteration count in a tight decrement sequence with aligned inner labels and an early exit for zero.
Halt delay returns immediately for zero length, otherwise repeatedly invokes the selected halt helper and remeasures with an ordered counter until elapsed time covers the request.

One halt helper targets a wake time formed from start plus length split into low and high halves using a deeper idle state; the other clamps the wait, monitors a per-CPU line, and requests no deep state with timer enable.
Microsecond and nanosecond delays scale through a common constant-delay helper that multiplies by loops-per-jiffy derived factors before invoking the indirect delay.
Timer readability reports true with a raw counter sample only when the main delay pointer is in timestamp mode, otherwise false without touching the output.
Error-injection override redirects the saved instruction pointer in the register frame to a plain return trampoline.
Checked user loads for one, two, four and eight bytes validate the address range, enable supervisor access to user memory, perform a zero-extending load, clear status, disable access and return.
Unchecked user loads omit range validation but issue a speculation barrier under supervisor access before the same sized zero-extending loads and status clearing.
User-load fault path disables supervisor access to user memory, zeroes the value register and returns a negative fault status.
Software population-count helpers reduce 32-bit and 64-bit inputs through mask, shift, add, multiply and final shift stages while preserving caller registers.
Register offset table maps sequential indices to general register slots in the trap frame, extended with eight extra 64-bit registers on 64-bit builds and four segment selectors otherwise.
Register role enumeration orders memory-reference, register, index and base roles starting at zero.
Diagnostics in the instruction evaluation unit use a fixed textual prefix identifying the subsystem.

Instruction fetch resolves the effective address from the register frame, copies up to the maximum instruction window from user space, and returns bytes obtained with an invalid-argument signal when address resolution fails.

No-operation classifier accepts same-register moves and zero-displacement address computations at native width, plain single-byte no-ops excluding extended encodings and repeat prefix, zero-target jumps, and a specific two-byte form; it rejects vector encodings and unknown map selectors.

Instruction decoding helpers bound-check upcoming bytes against a recorded end, fetch little-endian values of one, two or four bytes with cursor advance or peeking, and fail compilation for other widths.
Two static prefix sequences identify hypervisor emulation entry points for two platforms.
Relative-addressing test applies only in 64-bit mode after successful ModRM fetch and reports true when a ModRM byte is present with zero mode and base value five.
Memory-mapped I/O move helper is a type-parameterized inline string move that updates both destination and source operands and clobbers memory.
